L209@P5: 3.1. Numerical Verification of the Continuous Sandbox
L210@P5: This section aims to demonstrate, through large-scale Monte Carlo numerical simulations, how
L211@P5: the continuous dynamical sandbox naturally manifests the core statistical features of the 3x+1 map
L212@P5: without relying on any number-theoretic arithmetic rules—solely through geometric folding and

L216@P5: 3.1.1. Model Construction and Customized Markov Partition
L217@P5: When dealing with the symbolic dynamics of unimodal maps, traditional methods usually use
L218@P5: the critical point (extremum xc=0) as the boundary for the generating partition. However, to replicate
L219@P5: the microscopic arithmetic skeleton of the 3x+1 rules, we abandon this conventional approach.
L220@P5: Instead, targeting the Logistic map f(x)=1−μx2 in the period-3 window (μ≈1.7549), we propose a
L221@P5: customized non-generating partition based on the forward unstable fixed point x∗.
L222@P5: By solving the equation 1−μ(x∗)2=x∗, we determined the position of the unstable repellor in the
L223@P5: first quadrant to be x∗≈0.5219. Using this topological singularity as a threshold, we strictly partition
L224@P5: the phase space [−1,1] into two state intervals (Figure 2):
L225@P5: State 0 (Contraction State / Corresponding to Even): x∈[−1,x∗). Most of this interval is near the
L226@P5: origin, corresponding to dynamical dissipation and contraction (smaller absolute derivative).
L227@P5: State 1 (Expansion State / Corresponding to Odd): x∈[x∗,1]. This interval is near the edge of the
L228@P5: phase space, corresponding to momentary dynamical expansion (larger absolute derivative).
L229@P5: The physical significance of this customized partition is that it is not intended to maximize the
L230@P5: differentiation of initial orbital conditions, but rather to geometrically align perfectly with the oddeven operation mechanism in the 3x+1 problem.

L399@P11: 4. Discussion
L400@P11: 4.1. A Heuristic Pathway to a Theoretical Proof
L401@P11: In the discrete realm, proving the convergence of 3x+1 sequences is notoriously difficult due to
L402@P11: extreme pseudo-randomness and unpredictable local expansions. However, by transitioning to the

L404@P11: numerical trajectories. Instead, we can determine the macroscopic fate of the phase space through
L405@P11: two rigorous dynamical pillars:
L406@P11: Lyapunov Dissipation and Thermodynamic Collapse: The physical essence of the 3x+1 map
L407@P11: dictates a logarithmic expansion rate of ln3 for odd steps and a contraction rate of ln(0.5) for even
L408@P11: steps. Given our previously established 2:1 invariant measure, the theoretical expected rate is

L430@P12: 4.2. Implications for Other Number-Theoretic Enigmas
L431@P12: The methodology established in this study transcends the Collatz conjecture, offering a highly
L432@P12: generalizable computational physics paradigm for other intractable discrete mathematical problems.
L433@P12: Traditional analytic number theory frequently runs into micro-logical dead ends (such as the
L434@P12: “parity problem”) when confronting Diophantine equations or discrete sequences with strong
L435@P12: nonlinear jumps. By transforming discrete arithmetic rules into the continuous phase space of
L436@P12: autonomous or non-autonomous dynamical systems, we equip ourselves with a robust suite of
L437@P12: analytical tools: transfer operators, invariant measures, and renormalization flows.
L438@P12: This topological “stand-in” approach provides a blueprint for investigating other fundamental
L439@P12: discrete structures. For instance, analyzing the quasi-randomness and structural boundaries of prime
L440@P12: number distributions could potentially be recontextualized as the emergence of low-dimensional
L441@P12: deterministic chaos. Similarly, mapping discrete number-theoretic properties to the spectral
L442@P12: behaviors of chaotic maps opens new avenues for exploring spectral isomorphisms related to zeta
L443@P12: functions and their zeros. By converting pure algebraic riddles into the computation of operator
L444@P12: spectra and thermodynamic escape rates, this paradigm harnesses modern numerical computation
L445@P12: to bypass discrete roadblocks, serving as a powerful “probe” for the deepest enigmas in mathematics.
L446@P12: 5. Conclusions
L447@P12: This paper successfully translates the discrete, unpredictable 3x+1 number-theoretic problem
L448@P12: into a continuous, deterministic physical process. By constructing a customized Markov partition and
L449@P12: utilizing a Logistic dynamical sandbox locked in the period-3 window (μ≈1.7549), we established a
L450@P12: rigorous topological isomorphism between the two systems. Our numerical and theoretical
L451@P12: analyses—ranging from reproducing the “forbidden word 11” grammar to extracting the 2:1
L452@P12: invariant measure via the Perron-Frobenius transfer operator’s eigenspectrum—demonstrate that the
L453@P12: 3x+1 iteration and one-dimensional dissipative transient chaos belong to the same Universality
L454@P12: Class. Consequently, the Collatz conjecture is transformed from an arithmetic maze into an inevitable
L455@P12: thermodynamic collapse governed by Lyapunov dissipation and operator spectral gaps.
L456@P12: Methodologically, our greatest theoretical contribution lies in establishing continuous spectral
L457@P12: analysis as a macroscopic “probe” to bypass the micro-logical dead ends of traditional analytic
L458@P12: number theory, such as the “parity problem.” Instead of agonizing over the unpredictable trajectory
L459@P12: of a specific integer, we deploy high-precision numerical computation to analyze the transfer
L460@P12: operator of the isomorphic continuous sandbox. This approach acts as a “dimensionality reduction
L461@P12: strike,” where proving the existence of a spectral gap ( |λ2|<1 ) macroscopically eradicates the
L462@P12: possibility of infinite micro-level divergence. In the context of modern AI for Science (AI4S), massive
L463@P12: computation is thus repurposed from brute-force exhaustion into a genuine “physics mechanism
L464@P12: discoverer,” extracting continuous topological fossils from endless discrete data.
L465@P12: Ultimately, this research highlights the profound homologies between discrete mathematics and
L466@P12: continuous statistical physics. From the emergence of Riemann zeros in non-autonomous
L467@P12: renormalization flows to the collapse of 3x+1 cycles within simple autonomous parabolic folding,
L468@P12: nature embeds breathtaking dynamical structures at the lowest echelons of numbers. As AI-assisted
L469@P12: functional space approximation technologies and operator spectral theory continue to mature, this
L470@P12: interdisciplinary computational physics paradigm holds immense promise as a master key for
L471@P12: unlocking other century-old mathematical enigmas.
